connect.title: Connect a device
connect.intro: Scan this QR with your phone camera, or open the address below. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi.
connect.introTailscale: Scan this QR with your phone camera. The Tailscale address works from anywhere as long as the phone is on the same tailnet — it does not need the same Wi-Fi.
connect.autoNote: Accepting files without a prompt is configured in the Dashboard (PIN required).
connect.noteOwner: This page belongs to "{owner}". For two-way transfer, the second device must also
connect.noteOwnerRest: run its own LAN DROP — opening the page is not enough.
connect.statusUnavailable: Status could not be fetched from the server — check the connection.
connect.noAddress: No address detected. Make sure the device is on Wi-Fi, then reload the page.
connect.useForQr: Use this address for the QR
connect.checklist1: Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi (or one on Tailscale).
connect.checklist2: Both devices must run their own LAN DROP — opening the page alone is not enough, otherwise sending and receiving cannot work both ways.
connect.checklist3: The router/firewall must not block UDP 41234 and TCP 3000–3001.
connect.checklist4: If a device does not show up, check the "Network status" block above.
install.installed: Already installed on the home screen.
install.promptFailed: Could not open the install prompt
install.addToHome: Add LAN DROP to the home screen:
install.ios1: Open the Share menu (the box with an up arrow) in Safari.
install.ios3: Tap "Add" — the LAN DROP icon appears on your home screen.
install.android1: Tap the ⋮ button in the top right of the browser.
install.android3: Tap "Add" — the LAN DROP icon appears on your home screen.
install.desktop1: Click the install icon (⊕) in the Chrome address bar, or
install.desktop2: Open the browser menu → "Install" / "Install LAN DROP".
install.fullNote: Full install (works offline and opens when the server is slow) needs HTTPS. On a plain HTTP network, the add-to-home-screen button above still works.

dashboard.logNote: Logs live in server memory (last 300 lines). Restart clears them. Run the server with --debug to see everything in the terminal too.

dashboard.autoPeersNote: Device names must match exactly (case-sensitive) — a near-match sends the file to manual confirmation.
